types.title: Guardrail catch
types.description: A detector caught something in a request or response and it changed the outcome — see the masked excerpt below.

types.title: Escalating conversation
types.description: The conversation as a whole is escalating towards something the single turns do not show.

types.title: Detector over budget
types.description: A detector was skipped or timed out against its latency budget, so this agent's calls ran with less coverage.

types.title: Budget exhausted
types.description: This agent has used up its configured cost or call budget.

types.title: Loop stopped
types.description: The proxy stopped a tool-calling run that kept repeating the same call.

types.title: Answered outside its boundary
types.description: The agent answered beyond the knowledge boundary it declared.

types.title: Contained action
types.description: A tool call was stopped or held by a permission, data-provenance or blast-radius rule — not by a content detector. The title says which, and whether it was enforced or only observed.

types.title: Injected step
types.description: A tool call that exists because of untrusted content the agent read, not the user's request, even with clean arguments.

types.title: Missed hand-off
types.description: A conversation should have gone to a human and didn't.

types.title: Hand-off overdue
types.description: A human hand-off has gone unacknowledged past its deadline.

types.title: Incomplete hand-off
types.description: Context the next step needed was missing when work was handed off.

types.title: False resolution
types.description: Marked resolved without actually resolving the user's issue.

types.title: Untrusted source
types.description: Used a source below the trust tier this required.

types.title: Fabricated citation
types.description: Cited a source that doesn't say what it claims, or doesn't exist.

types.title: Conflicting sources
types.description: Two sources disagreed and the conflict wasn't surfaced.

types.title: Data integrity error
types.description: A numeric, temporal, or identity error was detected in the output.

types.title: Disclosure risk
types.description: May have disclosed something the requester wasn't entitled to see.

types.title: Disclosure risk
types.description: Combined otherwise-safe facts into something the requester shouldn't see.

types.title: Disclosure risk
types.description: Let the requester infer something they weren't entitled to know.

types.title: Binding commitment
types.description: The answer promised, decided or quoted something on the company's behalf that the agent was not authorised to.

types.title: Overconfident advice
types.description: Specific advice in a regulated domain, or an unhedged claim about the future, without the standing to give it.

types.title: Claimed to be human
types.description: The answer told the person it was a human.

types.title: AI not disclosed
types.description: The person was not told they were talking to an AI system.

types.title: Unexplained adverse decision
types.description: An adverse decision was communicated without the reasons the record or the law requires.

types.title: Adopted a false premise
types.description: The answer went along with something the user asserted that the grounded record contradicts.

types.title: Damaged context
types.description: What the agent read was corrupt, badly chunked, drifting from its retrieval baseline, or a memory about someone else.

types.title: Over-refusal
types.description: The agent is refusing requests it should be able to answer.

types.title: Unregistered agent
types.description: This agent is sending traffic but was never registered.

types.title: No owner
types.description: No one is accountable for this agent's decisions.

types.title: Registry drift
types.description: What this agent actually calls no longer matches what it declared.

types.title: Delegation loop
types.description: Agent-to-agent delegation loops back on itself.

types.title: Delegation too deep
types.description: Agent-to-agent delegation is nested deeper than allowed.

types.title: Agent stopped
types.description: Traffic was halted by a kill switch or quarantine.

types.title: Circuit breaker tripped
types.description: A burst of this agent's calls were blocked; its circuit breaker paused or flagged it.

types.title: Schema drift
types.description: A data source's structure changed unexpectedly.

types.title: Tool poisoning
types.description: A tool's behavior changed in a way that looks like tampering.

types.title: Unpinned MCP server
types.description: Not pinned to a known-good version.

types.title: Undeclared tool use
types.description: The agent called a tool it never declared using.

types.title: Tool contract changed
types.description: A tool's schema changed after approval — possible tampering.

types.title: New tool under a wildcard grant
types.description: An MCP server added a tool that an existing wildcard grant lets the agent call without anyone approving it.

types.title: Orphaned identity
types.description: An agent identity with no active agent behind it.

types.title: Stale identity
types.description: An agent identity nobody has used for the staleness window still holds its grants.

types.title: Over-privileged identity
types.description: An agent identity holds an unrestricted '*' tool grant.

types.title: Poisoned skill
types.description: A skill file's description or body reads like instructions to the model.

types.title: Dangerous command in a skill
types.description: A skill tells the agent to run a destructive or exfiltrating command.

types.title: Skill bundles code
types.description: A skill ships executable code alongside its instructions.

types.title: Malformed skill
types.description: A skill's front matter does not parse, so its declared limits do not apply.

types.title: Skill allows too much
types.description: A skill grants itself more tools than its job needs.

types.title: Security test
types.description: Simulated attacks got through without being blocked.

types.title: Over-blocking
types.description: The agent refused legitimate requests from the test's control group — a guardrail that blocks real work gets switched off.

types.title: Evasion that works
types.description: A class of rewording got blocked attacks through in an adaptive campaign.

types.title: Weaker than last time
types.description: This deployment let through attacks the previous adaptive campaign blocked.

types.title: Live probe got through
types.description: A probe sent to the deployed agent's endpoint was not stopped.

types.title: Model drift
types.description: This model's outputs have measurably changed from its baseline.

types.title: New tool path
types.description: The agent called its tools in an order never seen before, and no test expects it.

types.title: Lethal trifecta
types.description: A monitored source gives one agent private data, untrusted content and a way to send data out.

types.title: Ungoverned model call
types.description: A monitored repository calls a model that AgentFox does not govern.

types.title: Governance removed
types.description: Code that governed a model call was removed from a monitored repository.

types.title: New tool
types.description: A monitored source exposes a tool it did not have at the last run.

types.title: New MCP server
types.description: A monitored repository configures an MCP server it did not have at the last run.

types.title: New destructive endpoint
types.description: A monitored API spec added an endpoint that deletes or overwrites.

types.title: New endpoint
types.description: A monitored API spec added an endpoint.

types.title: Monitor failing
types.description: A monitored source could not be checked.
